scenes.title: Hello from Chad and Ewa

verification.gui: Production metadata only; no filming or audio generation performed.

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.text: Hello, I'm Chad G. P. Taylor. Welcome to creating tokens in Dash Evolution. We'll build a small draft, then work through what its owners and holders would actually be allowed to do.

turns.speaker: learner
turns.text: And I'm Ewa Dashwood. I want to understand the choices that survive my enthusiasm, especially the permanent ones.

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.text: A sensible precaution. This presentation is generated by AI and may contain mistakes. We'll check the application and explain what still needs a live network check. My confidence is not one of the validation steps.

turns.speaker: learner
turns.text: Good. Let's keep the explanations friendly and the settings precise.

scenes.title: One workspace, six chapters
scenes.screen: Chapter overview, then the seven section labels. No paid operation.

verification.gui: Seven-section navigation observed across the coordinator checks; no recording performed.

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.text: The creator has seven sections: Basics, Supply and permissions, Distribution, Groups, History, Search and documents, and Review. Our six chapters give the longer subjects room to breathe.

turns.speaker: learner
turns.text: So the chapter numbers won't always match the section numbers?

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.text: Correct. First we prepare a fixed-supply example. Then we explore a more flexible draft, including every rule and all eight recurring formulas. Finally we inspect the exact contract and the registration gates.

turns.speaker: learner
turns.text: And a successful draft isn't a successful registration. We'll only describe a network result as observed when there is evidence for it.

turns.speaker: learner
turns.text: Do I need a funded account just to explore the form?

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.text: No. Drafting is available without an identity. Use Testnet for this lesson. In Review, preparation needs a loaded identity and an available authentication key with High or Critical security, plus access to its signing material.

turns.speaker: learner
turns.text: The identity's Platform credits pay creation fees, rather than the token's own balance?

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.text: Exactly. Unlock a wallet only when required, away from the camera. Preparation checks the current owner and key over the network. Loading an identity does not prove that its key is usable or that it has enough credits.

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.text: Also let the application finish synchronizing its Core, SPV and quorum data. An internet connection alone is not enough. In our pinned-build walkthrough, the first Check settings stopped because that network verification data was not ready; connect and let synchronization finish before checking again.

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.text: Enter CloudCredit as the Token name, and CloudCredits as the Plural name. Both fields are required; this form does not invent the plural for us.

turns.speaker: learner

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.text: Not here. Names need at least three characters without spaces and must fit within twenty-five UTF-8 bytes. Accented or other multibyte characters use more of that byte allowance.

turns.speaker: learner
turns.text: So the displayed name is a label, not a unique token address. We'll use the full identifiers when we need to distinguish tokens later.

turns.speaker: learner

turns.speaker: teacher

turns.speaker: learner

turns.speaker: teacher

turns.speaker: learner

scenes.title: What fixed supply promises
scenes.screen: Supply & permissions: select All 13 rules; inspect every fixed rule and the cap consequence. Distribution is off, Groups is empty, and all six histories are on.

verification.gui: Evidence: fixed-online-prepare (observed). See the pinned ledger for exact scope; other scene controls remain source checked only.

turns.speaker: learner
turns.text: What makes this more than a token with a reassuring name?

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.text: Its maximum equals its initial supply, and all thirteen action rules have no performer, no administrator, and all three change allowances off. No one can mint more, freeze holders, pause transfers, or change those rules through these permissions.

turns.speaker: learner
turns.text: Ordinary transfers can still be enabled. The absence of issuer powers isn't the absence of holder transfers.

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.text: Correct. And a cap always limits outstanding supply, not the number ever minted over the token's lifetime. Our fixed example also disables burning and later minting; we'll discuss that distinction in the owner-managed draft.

turns.speaker: learner
turns.text: What would count as confirmation?

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.text: The Token created receipt contains identifiers from the accepted contract, together with the owner and initial allocation. Prepared IDs or a broadcast alone do not prove creation.

turns.speaker: learner
turns.text: Then we copy the confirmed Contract ID and Token ID, and use Open contract to inspect the result. We check the intended recipient rather than assuming every allocation belongs to the issuer.

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.text: Yes. Create another token starts a fresh creator after a confirmed result. Until that branch has been observed, this is a description of the expected receipt, not a claim that we've created CloudCredit.

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.text: The English singular name remains included because we marked it searchable. Keywords are lowercased and deduplicated. There can be at most fifty distinct terms, each three to fifty UTF-8 bytes after lowercasing, without spaces or control characters.

turns.speaker: learner

scenes.title: Precision without a hundredfold mistake
scenes.screen: Supply & permissions: show Decimal places = 2 and amount conversions. Change to 3 and back. Demonstrate an unrepresentable fractional amount, then correct it.

verification.gui: Evidence: precision-change (observed), supply-switches (observed). See the pinned ledger for exact scope; other scene controls remain source checked only.

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.text: Decimal places can range from zero to sixteen. Two means one hundred base units per token; zero means whole tokens only.

turns.speaker: learner
turns.text: If I change precision, should I manually multiply the token amount?

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.text: No. The editor preserves the displayed token amount while recalculating its base units. It does not silently round an amount that the new precision cannot represent. Invalid text remains available to correct.

turns.speaker: learner
turns.text: We'll finish at two decimals: one thousand tokens is one hundred thousand base units, and the ten-thousand cap is one million base units. The same distinction will matter in the emission formulas.

scenes.title: Transfers, pauses and frozen recipients
scenes.screen: Supply & permissions: toggle the three transfer-state checkboxes and inspect their consequences. Restore Allow transfers between holders on, Start with transfers paused off, and Allow transfers to frozen identities off.

verification.gui: Evidence: supply-switches (observed). See the pinned ledger for exact scope; other scene controls remain source checked only.

checks: Show warning with pause authority disabled, then restore the owner pause authority and final booleans.

turns.speaker: learner
turns.text: Allow transfers between holders sounds more permanent than Start with transfers paused.

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.text: It is. Transferability cannot change after creation, and disabling it requires protocol fourteen or later. Pausing is a separate initial state; a permitted pause-or-resume action can later resume transfers.

turns.speaker: learner
turns.text: The form warns if we start paused with nobody able to resume. And distributions or other configured actions can continue while transfers are paused.

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.text: Allow transfers to frozen identities controls receiving only; a frozen identity still cannot spend. We'll restore ordinary transfers on, starting paused off, and receiving while frozen off.

verification.gui: Evidence: history-controls (observed). See the pinned ledger for exact scope; other scene controls remain source checked only.

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.text: History has six independent event histories: transfers, freezes and unfreezes, mints, burns, direct-pricing changes, and direct purchases.

turns.speaker: learner
turns.text: Turning one off gives the parent checkbox a mixed state. Keep all six histories selects them together again.

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.text: These settings concern the contract's event histories. They do not hide the contract, make transactions private, or grant permission to perform the corresponding actions.

turns.speaker: learner
turns.text: We'll keep all six for our final token, even where a related action is disabled. Records and authority answer different questions.

turns.speaker: learner
turns.text: These five protocol templates aren't the same as the two examples above them?

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.text: Correct. Compare Most restrictive, Emergency action, Minting and burning, Extreme actions, and All advanced actions separately. Each is a proposal with a full comparison, not an immediate overwrite.

turns.speaker: learner

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.text: And Extreme actions adds broad rule-change allowances and main-group replacement authority. Read the complete performer, administrator and three-allowance matrix for each template. We'll cancel these comparisons and keep our deliberately limited draft.

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.text: Supply and permissions always contains thirteen action rules. The filters show all rules, enabled powers, or changeable rules; a filter does not change the contract.

turns.speaker: learner

scenes.screen: In the rule editor, inspect the administrator and all three Later changes flags. Temporarily select Contract owner and toggle each allowance, then restore No one and all flags off. Demonstrate Open Groups.
controls: Allow the administrator to remove all action performers
Allow the administrator to remove all rule administrators

verification.gui: Evidence: rule-0 (observed). See the pinned ledger for exact scope; other scene controls remain source checked only.

turns.speaker: learner
turns.text: The administrator controls who holds the action, rather than automatically being its performer?

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.text: Yes. Three separate allowances let the administrator remove all action performers, remove all rule administrators, or replace itself. Those flags are not one master permission switch.

turns.speaker: learner
turns.text: If the performer is No one but an administrator remains, the action might be enabled later. And if the administrator is No one, there's currently nobody to use these allowances.

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.text: Exactly. For our final draft, every rule administrator will be No one and all three allowances off. Open Groups takes us to the group editor; it doesn't create or assign a group automatically.

scenes.title: Lock the outstanding-supply ceiling
scenes.screen: Supply & permissions: edit Change maximum supply. Set performer and administrator to No one and all three allowances off. Inspect the permanent hard-cap notice.

verification.gui: Evidence: rule-6 (observed). See the pinned ledger for exact scope; other scene controls remain source checked only.

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.text: To make the ten-thousand ceiling permanent, inspect Change maximum supply. Its performer and administrator are both No one, and all three change allowances are off.

turns.speaker: learner
turns.text: A number in Maximum outstanding supply alone would not prove a permanent cap if somebody could later raise it.

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.text: Right. The notice distinguishes a hard cap from a changeable limit. It also distinguishes both from No maximum supply.

turns.speaker: learner
turns.text: And burning can free capacity below an outstanding-supply cap. The cap is not a lifetime counter of every token ever minted.

scenes.screen: Inspect Mint additional tokens. Show Contract owner, Specific identity and No fixed destination as default recipient choices. Restore owner and enable Allow choosing a recipient on each mint.
controls: Default recipient for newly created tokens

turns.speaker: learner
turns.text: Mint additional tokens lets the permitted performer create more, within the outstanding-supply limit.

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.text: Yes. The default recipient for newly created tokens also receives the initial supply. We can choose the owner or a specific identity. No fixed destination removes the fixed destination for future minting; the initial allocation still falls back to the owner.

turns.speaker: learner
turns.text: Allow choosing a recipient on each mint is a separate choice. It doesn't grant minting power by itself.

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.text: We'll use the owner as default recipient, permit the owner to mint, and enable per-mint recipient choice for our final custom example. Recheck the Initial allocation line after changing the destination.

scenes.title: Lock the two destination policies
scenes.screen: Edit Change the default mint recipient and Change per-mint recipient choice separately. Set both performers and administrators to No one and all flags off, while keeping Allow choosing a recipient on each mint on.

verification.gui: Evidence: rule-9 (observed), rule-10 (observed). See the pinned ledger for exact scope; other scene controls remain source checked only.

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.text: There are two rules behind those destination settings: Change the default mint recipient, and Change per-mint recipient choice.

turns.speaker: learner
turns.text: So allowing a different recipient on each mint is not the same as allowing someone to change whether that option exists.

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.text: Exactly. We'll lock both policy-changing rules with no performer, no administrator and all allowances off. The chosen owner destination and enabled per-mint choice remain the values we reviewed.

turns.speaker: learner
turns.text: I can now explain both the current setting and who could alter it. That's considerably better than saying, 'I clicked the destination thing.'

scenes.title: Burning the performer’s own tokens
scenes.screen: Edit Burn own tokens: performer Contract owner, administrator No one, all three flags off. Do not execute a burn.

verification.gui: Evidence: rule-1 (observed). See the pinned ledger for exact scope; other scene controls remain source checked only.

turns.speaker: learner
turns.text: Does allowing the owner to burn mean the owner can delete anyone's balance?

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.text: No. This rule is Burn own tokens. It permits burning from the acting identity's own balance; it is not confiscation from another holder.

turns.speaker: learner
turns.text: Our owner can mint and burn its own tokens, but the permanent outstanding cap still constrains future supply.

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.text: Correct. We'll retain owner as performer, no administrator, and all change allowances off. We're configuring that power here, not performing a burn.

scenes.title: Freeze and unfreeze are separate
scenes.screen: Edit Freeze an account, then Unfreeze an account. Inspect their actor choices and restore both rules permanently off. Revisit Allow transfers to frozen identities and leave it off.

verification.gui: Evidence: rule-2 (observed), rule-3 (observed), supply-switches (observed). See the pinned ledger for exact scope; other scene controls remain source checked only.

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.text: Freezing prevents a holder from spending. Unfreezing is a separate power, so enabling one doesn't automatically provide the other.

turns.speaker: learner
turns.text: That's a potentially awkward combination if someone can freeze a balance and nobody can release it.

turns.speaker: teacher
turns.text: Exactly. The receiving-while-frozen checkbox controls incoming transfers, not the ability to spend. Read all three choices together.

turns.speaker: learner
turns.text: For our final token, freeze and unfreeze both have no performer or administrator, with all allowances off. Receiving while frozen stays off too.
